title: Cornell 'Jane Doe' Terrified After Swatting Incident and Violent Threats Following Sexual Assault Lawsuit
snippet: The anonymous former student suing Cornell University over an alleged 2024 fraternity gang rape is living in fear after an armed police 'swatting' swarm at her family home and mounting death threats.
content:
A former Cornell University student who recently filed a explosive lawsuit against the university and a fraternity over an alleged gang rape is now living in extreme fear after her family home was targeted in a dangerous swatting incident this week, according to her attorney.

The victim, publicly identified only as Jane Doe, filed a 101-page civil complaint last month alleging she was drugged and sexually assaulted by members of the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024. But in the weeks since coming forward, her legal action has triggered an overwhelming wave of harassment, doxxing, and explicit death threats.

Armed Cops Swarm Family Residence

The harassment reached a terrifying climax on Tuesday evening when a fraudulent 911 call dispatched armed officers to Doe's family residence. The anonymous caller falsely claimed a gunman had killed two family members inside the house.

According to police reports and Doe's attorney, Thomas Giuffra, officers arrived with weapons drawn, confronting Doe's brother and boyfriend as they backed out of the driveway. Her father was also held at gunpoint after stepping out of the front door to investigate the commotion.

"If you had a trigger-happy cop, or somebody had done the wrong thing, somebody could have ended up dead," Giuffra said, noting that the FBI and local law enforcement are actively investigating the hoax caller.

Chilling Threats and Doxxing Campaign

Giuffra disclosed that the swatting incident occurred immediately after Doe received an unsettling phone call from an unknown individual claiming to share a name with one of her alleged assailants. Her attorney's office also received a recorded voicemail on Wednesday warning that "blood will be shed" unless Doe drops her lawsuit.

The harassment has not been limited to phone calls. High-profile social media figures have attempted to uncover and publish Doe's real identity online, a practice known as doxxing. Doe has also received text messages containing gun emojis, prompting her to tape paper over the windows of her childhood home to block the view from the street.

"Before this week, it was just a lunatic fringe, which you can be dismissive of," Giuffra noted. "Now it’s somebody taking real steps to harm you, and that’s pretty frightening."

Campus Outrage and Derailed Aspirations

Doe had originally intended to pursue a career in hospitality after studying at Cornell's prestigious Nolan School of Hotel Administration. However, the emotional toll of the alleged assault and the subsequent institutional failure forced her to leave the university without graduating. She has since abandoned her career pursuits in New York City to isolate herself with family.

Meanwhile, the lawsuit has sparked widespread anger across Cornell's Ithaca campus, where students held a seven-hour sit-in this week in solidarity with Doe. Demonstrators are protesting the university's and local authorities' initial handling of the sexual assault allegations.

In response to the growing backlash, Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff acknowledged the student body's anger during a campus meeting, while the university announced that former acting U.S. Attorney General Sally Yates has been tapped to conduct an independent review of how the institution handles sexual assault claims.
